title: Crypto markets fall as Binance investigates breach; portfolio declines 3.9%
paragraphs: Bitcoin and Ethereum fell as selling spread across major cryptocurrencies. Proactive reported Bitcoin near $77,100, down almost 5% over 24 hours, and Ethereum around $2,220, down roughly 5.5%. XRP and Solana lost about 7%, while BNB fell nearly 8%. Total crypto market value stood near $2.61 trillion. The weakness was broad, although Hyperliquid gained about 14%. Binance's security incident adds a major operational concern to an already weak market.

Binance estimated the impact of unauthorized withdrawals at about $6.3 billion and said roughly $3 billion had been frozen on-chain. It temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals and pledged to cover losses using its SAFU fund and company resources. Its preliminary investigation points to a compromised employee laptop, with the technical investigation still underway. TRM Labs separately traced approximately $6.36 billion leaving wallets across ten blockchains. The immediate issue for customers is access to funds while security checks and recovery work continue.

The Bank of Japan kept its policy rate around 1.25% in an 8-1 vote, with the dissenter seeking 1.5%. It also approved faster sales of its equity ETFs, increasing the annual pace at book value from about 330 billion yen to 860 billion yen starting in January 2027. That is a further withdrawal of central-bank support for financial markets. For crypto, it matters as part of the global funding backdrop, without establishing the cause of this sell-off.

Coinbase's new quarterly results showed $1.2 billion in revenue and $719 million in net income, with much of the profit coming from unrealized gains on investment holdings. Stablecoin revenue rose 5% from the previous quarter to $307 million, while average USDC held in Coinbase products reached $22 billion. Prediction markets exceeded a $200 million annualized revenue pace. These figures show payments, stablecoins and newer trading products becoming meaningful revenue sources, even as overall crypto trading volumes fell 10% during the quarter.

Our two on-chain wallets total about $71,277: $11,843 in the active treasury and $59,434 in the Safe. That is $2,916 lower, or 3.9%, than the previous archived update. The Safe's 26.74 million directly held ARC tokens are unchanged in quantity and worth about $46,839, roughly 66% of the combined portfolio. WETH/ARC liquidity pools add about $10,371 of exposure to that pair. ARC concentration remains the largest portfolio risk, alongside ETH exposure and protocol risk.

Treasury Beefy positions are worth about $1,740, down from $3,332, while assets held directly in that wallet rose from $5,353 to $6,622. Its visible balances now include about 1,063 USDC, 3.25 cbHYPE and 128 eUSD.

Aave debt totals about $3,140 against $7,633 of supplied WETH. Treasury and Safe health factors fell from 2.42 to 2.33 and from 1.94 to 1.86, respectively. The smaller Fluid position has about $1,062 of debt, $153 of net value and a 1.03 health factor, leaving a narrow liquidation buffer.
